observed_user_feedback: Current Crystal Workbench is technically functional but the user cannot understand the interface at a glance.
screenshot_findings: The top navigation exposes implementation/data concepts directly: Overview, Assortment, Materials, Accessories, Packaging, References, Design Board.
The home page begins with raw database counts such as materials, variants, components and assets, which are meaningful to the system but not useful as the user's first decision surface.
Internal enum labels such as minerals_crystals, pearls_organic, hardware_accessories, A_CORE, B_DESIGN_EXTENSION and C_SIGNATURE_ONE_OF_ONE are shown literally.
Cards have large empty areas and weak action hierarchy; it is unclear what the user should click first.
The information architecture separates Materials, Accessories and Packaging even though the user's actual mental model is selecting things for a design.
The interface is English-first even though the user operates this project primarily in Chinese.
The current overview behaves like a database dashboard rather than a design workbench.
design_principle: Task-oriented, Chinese-first, human-readable. Hide database terminology unless the user explicitly opens a technical detail view.

visual_direction.density: compact but readable; no large empty cards

acceptance_examples: A first-time user can understand within 10 seconds that the main workflows are 选品、灵感、设计.
No raw enum such as minerals_crystals or A_CORE is visible in the default UI.
No raw database counts dominate the homepage.
The user can reach any material category from 选品库 without understanding canonical DB concepts.
Technical canonical/candidate status remains available only in secondary detail when useful.
All existing sidecar and read-only database safety guarantees remain unchanged.
